templates.header: Duration: {duration} minutes. Starting checkpoint: {prev_tag}. Ending checkpoint: {tag} ({hash}).
templates.access_before: Learners need two things: their own project repository in the course GitLab group on gitlab.ciklum.net, and the
templates.access_after: in the public course repository, which holds the starter project and, for each lesson, the given files and the check pack. Learners build their own implementation; the reference checkpoints in the same repository are the instructor's answer key.
templates.agent_role: Your coding agent handles preparation, implementation and execution. You set the scope, inspect its changes and explain the evidence. This development assistant is separate from the investigation agents inside the platform.
templates.prepare_prompt: Prepare my learner project for Lesson {nn}. Open my project repository in my course GitLab group on gitlab.ciklum.net, cloning it into ~/agentic-course/my-platform if it is not there, and confirm it holds my completed {prev_tag} work with all its checks passing. Update my read-only copy of the course repository in ~/agentic-course/course, cloning it from https://github.com/maxvpavlov/ciklum-innovate-l3-2026 if it is missing; its learner-kit folder is the course kit. Use the pinned Python 3.12 environment and the offline mock provider. Do not add this lesson's work yet. Report the project location, its current checkpoint, the test results and any missing prerequisites. Do not ask me to run terminal commands.
templates.orient_intro: Next, have the coding agent read this lesson's check pack and add it to the project before any code is written.
templates.orient_prompt: Read learner-kit/lessons/{nn} in the course repository: its README, the given files and the check pack. Copy the whole given files and the check pack into my project exactly as the README says, without changing them, and commit that; a given definition that must be pasted into a module is added in the build step that creates or changes that module. Then run the tests and report what fails and why: at first this lesson's test file may fail to import, because the modules it needs do not exist yet. List the interfaces my code must provide, with the exact names, signatures, fields and error codes the tests use, and the capability they verify. Explain the implementation sequence before we begin. Do not write the implementation yet, and do not look for or use a finished solution.
templates.readiness: Rehearse the session with a learner project built from the course kit, so you see what learners see: the check pack fails until each capability is built. The reference checkpoint remains your answer key for the excerpts below. In class, use one bounded prompt at a time; learners inspect the change, explain the control decision and review the check evidence.
templates.offline: Have the coding agent use the offline mock provider for class. If live access fails, restore that configuration and continue. Keep credentials in secure configuration. Adapter request shapes were tested with mock HTTP; live account access was not exercised.
templates.pinned: Pinned versions in pyproject.toml and uv.lock: Python 3.12, MCP 2.2.0, A2A SDK 1.1.2, httpx 0.28.1, FastAPI 0.141.1, uvicorn 0.52.4, jsonschema 4.26.0, pytest 9.1.1 and pytest-asyncio 1.4.0. Have the coding agent manage their installation.
templates.script_intro: Use SAY for instructor narration, SHOW and REVIEW for the code and evidence participants examine, PROMPT for text they give their coding agents, and PAUSE for discussion. Prompts define scope and expected behaviour; the agent handles command execution. Code excerpts remain as reading and review material from the exact reference checkpoint, not manual typing instructions.
templates.opening_show: The coding agent’s baseline report, current learner project, synthetic incident records and lesson outcome. Ask participants to explain what already works before authorizing the next bounded change.
templates.concept_pause: Invite one learner to trace the control flow and another to identify a failure boundary. Resolve different interpretations before opening the implementation.
templates.step_show: The current learner implementation and {file}. Use the following prompt to make the bounded change, then inspect the agent’s result.
templates.step_prompt: For Lesson {nn}, continue in my learner project. {body} Build to the interfaces the Lesson {nn} check pack uses, and do not edit the check pack or the given files. Preserve earlier behaviour, run relevant checks and show the change and observed evidence. Stop at this step.
templates.review: Compare the coding agent’s change with this reference excerpt. It covers source lines {start} to {end} at {tag}; common indentation is reduced for display. Ask the agent to explain material differences in behaviour.
templates.step_pause: Have learners identify the boundary in their agent’s change and explain the expected failure behaviour. Compare it with the reference excerpt before accepting the change.
templates.exercise_prompt: Help me carry out the Lesson {nn} learner exercise in my existing project: {body} First state the expected outcomes, then run the experiment in a throwaway script outside tests/, or from a clean Git state you can restore. Show the observed results and explain any discrepancy. Keep the original acceptance criteria and restore temporary experiments when finished.
templates.verify: Give the coding agent the verification prompt below, then inspect its evidence and explain the result in your own words.
templates.verify_prompt: Verify my Lesson {nn} implementation against its completion criteria. Update the checkpoint indicator in incident/__init__.py to {n} only when the required capability is present. Run the full test suite, which includes the Lesson {nn} check pack and every earlier lesson's tests, and then the Session {nn} demonstration with python -m incident.lab {n}, all unchanged and using the offline provider (MODEL_PROVIDER unset or set to mock). Confirm that the passing count matches the one in the Lesson {nn} check pack README. Keep the expected outcomes unchanged. Report checks actually executed, failures, relevant output and any untested integration. Explain the result, then commit my work and push it to my repository on gitlab.ciklum.net; if glab is also signed in to other GitLab hosts, make sure the push goes to gitlab.ciklum.net. Do not equate an unrun or skipped check with a pass.
templates.expected_behaviour: The coding agent returns actual check results and the demonstration’s structured output. Run identifiers and elapsed times vary. Compare the status and capability outcomes with the recorded reference below, and investigate differences.
templates.practice_pause: Ask learners to explain the evidence before accepting the checkpoint. If a check fails, use the specific recovery prompt below and review the resulting correction.
templates.recorded: The independently unpacked {tag} checkpoint passed its full test suite and this lesson demo, and so does the Lesson {nn} check pack from the course kit. Recorded test result: {passed} passed in {seconds}s. Learners commit and push their checkpoint to their GitLab repository; {tag} ({hash}) remains the instructor's answer key.
templates.files_intro: In the reference, this checkpoint changed the files below. Learners write the implementation files themselves; the lab, the tests and any given files arrive in the Lesson {nn} check pack. Ask the agent to explain any additional file changes it needs.
templates.review_prompt: Review my completed Lesson {nn} work against the Lesson {nn} check pack and completion criteria. Show the files I changed and the interfaces I provide, and explain how each completion criterion is met with code or test evidence. Point out the design choices I made that the check pack does not force, and what each one costs or gains. Preserve deliberate improvements and earlier capabilities.
templates.recovery_prompt: I am working on Lesson {nn}. The symptom is: {symptom} Diagnostic focus: {diagnostic} Recovery guidance: {recovery} Reproduce the issue, make the smallest necessary correction and rerun affected checks. Report the cause, changed files and observed outcome. Preserve security controls and acceptance criteria.
templates.discussion: Which decision would change for a larger or more sensitive workload, and what additional evidence would you require before changing it? Tie the answer to the code, the task requirements and the acceptance checks.

verification_scope.tested: All course tags were independently unpacked and tested. The completed repository has 53 passing tests. Real local MCP stdio, the tool gateway's shared sessions and pinned definitions, A2A HTTP discovery, streaming, delegated-token authentication and cancellation were exercised. The platform console was driven in a headless Chromium browser against every checkpoint from lesson-08 onward.
verification_scope.not_tested: Live model credentials, paid provider calls, live model judging, third-party MCP or A2A services, remote MCP OAuth, an enterprise identity provider, a managed secret vault, production cloud rollout and an external observability collector were not tested. The offline provider is a deterministic fixture, so its usage and quality results are teaching measurements. Read TESTING.md for the full scope and environment details.
verification_scope.local_effects: The SQLite mock-effect ledger proves its local transaction boundary. It does not guarantee exactly-once effects for arbitrary external APIs. The A2A specialist task store is in memory. The restricted Compose sandbox uses temporary writable state; persistent deployment storage requires separate configuration and validation.
verification_scope.platform_identity: Tokens are HMAC-signed with one shared development key so the course runs offline; a production issuer signs asymmetrically and publishes verification keys. The credential store keeps values in process memory and is not a vault. The gateway runs in the platform process; production gateways are usually separate network services.

learner_prompts.title: Coding agent prompts for the course
intro: Each learner builds their own platform in their own repository in the course GitLab group on gitlab.ciklum.net, by prompting a coding agent. The learner kit in the public course repository (https://github.com/maxvpavlov/ciklum-innovate-l3-2026/tree/main/learner-kit) supplies the starter project and, for every lesson, the given files and a check pack of tests that fail until the capability is built. It contains no solutions. The agent handles setup, repository operations, execution and verification. You set scope, inspect code and decide whether the observed evidence meets the lesson criteria.

These prompts guide a learner implementation; a coding agent’s completion message is not proof that its result passed the checks. Use offline fixtures unless you deliberately configure and authorize a live integration.
learner_prompts.references: Course kit: learner-kit/lessons/{nn}. Instructor answer key: {prev_tag} to {tag}.

platform_components: Agent runtime: bounded ReAct loop, typed run state, event log
Tool contracts, approval boundary, MCP transport and the first console
Context selection, retrieval, memory and versioned artifacts
Durable runs, crash recovery and exact-action approval
Supervisor, scoped subagents and parallel coordination
Platform core: agent registry, durable run API, registry and approval views
MCP tool gateway: policy, audit and shared upstream sessions
Agent identity, delegated credentials and credential store
Operations: traces, admission control and evaluated releases
Tuning, before/after evidence and the capstone presentation
